in an interview Sunday, as he seeks to turn around a disappointing performance at the unit.

spending on conventional exploration and appraisal activity plunged 36% to$1.82B between 2021 and 2025 compared to the previous five-year period, according to data from Wood Mackenzie, and McLachlan was recruited from TotalEnergies last year to replicate the E&P turnaround he achieved at the French company.
"Two years ago... we drilled 10 wells. Next year, we've got a program of 20 exploration wells and probably... 5-6 appraisal wells on top of that. So it's a significant increase," McLachlan told
in his first interview since taking the role last November.

"We needed to increase the spend because we just didn't have the exposure," McLachlan said. "So we've increased our spend on seismic data, which is the enabling piece of how to generate prospects, without which you can't generate ideas."

Exploration teams led by McLachlan at TotalEnergies won the "most admired explorer" atWood Mackenzie's annual exploration awards in 2020, 2021, and 2023, and scored the "Discovery of the Year" award in 2023 for the Venus discovery offshore Namibia, one of thelargest offshore discoveries made in the past decade.
has doubled its total exploration acreage since 2024, amd the company is making more and larger bets to find oil and gas.
interview, McLachlan pointed to several hotspots of activity including Namibia, Guyana, Guinea-Bissau, and Egypt but cautioned against a tendency to try to "pick winners."
"We're looking to build new businesses. This isn't just about one good opportunity," McLachlan said, "You have to execute a program. You need statistics on your side."
